observations.observation: The event occurred on Sept. 16, 2026. The earliest exact-time primary dissemination found is onsemi’s 2:30 PM EDT release (18:30Z); the full financial slide deck was filed by 4:02:25 PM EDT (20:02:25Z). The Elec report arrived on Sept. 30 at 04:36:13Z, shortly before cutoff, so it is a later recap rather than the initial source.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The Investor Day may have disclosed figures live earlier; the retrieved dated records do not establish the precise first-spoken time of each figure.

observations.observation: The deck states 2026E revenue of $6.5B and a 12–14% revenue CAGR from 2026E through 2030, alongside 38% operating-margin and 30–35% free-cash-flow-margin targets. The Elec’s roughly $10.2–11.0B 2030 revenue range is consistent with compounding the stated base and CAGR over four years; it is not a standalone exact revenue point target in the deck.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The deck’s future margins and cash-flow measures are non-GAAP forward-looking targets, not realized results; onsemi cautions against relying on them alone.

observations.observation: AI-data-center growth was already part of the pre-event context: in August, onsemi reported Q2 revenue growth and said it expected AI-data-center revenue to more than double in 2026. The Sept. 16 addition was a longer-term 2030 target framework.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The 2026 AI-data-center expectation was management guidance; it did not establish realized 2030 revenue.

observations.observation: The prior corporate plan cited 10–12% revenue CAGR for 2022–2027. A pre-event report attributed an 11–13% 2030 growth model to Wells Fargo; onsemi’s new 12–14% 2026E–2030 target overlaps that reported model. The older corporate plan and newer model use different bases and horizons, and the Wells Fargo report is not marketwide consensus.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The sell-side model is one reported analyst estimate; it cannot stand in for consensus.

observations.observation: The historical base was mixed: onsemi reported 2025 revenue below 2024, while Q2 2026 revenue was up year over year. A Sept. 17 report of Stifel commentary said the long-term model could be below expectations and that near-/mid-term margin progression remained unclear.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The Stifel item is a single analyst view; historical results and commentary do not determine whether future targets will be met.

observations.observation: The physical-AI strategy had a material pre-event corporate transaction context: onsemi had announced a proposed Synaptics acquisition in June, with a stated mid-2027 expected close subject to approvals. That was an agreement, not completed integration or realized synergies by cutoff.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The closing timeline and benefits were forward-looking and conditional.

observations.observation: The searched onsemi disclosure concerns semiconductor, sensing, and system-level power products. It does not identify Bloom Energy, an Energy Server project, a Bloom order, or Bloom deployment data; it should not be treated as direct evidence of Bloom-specific demand or execution.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The news concerns onsemi’s own addressable markets and targets; it supplies no evidence of customer allocation to Bloom.

gaps: The precise time when Investor Day speakers first stated the 2030 financial assumptions is not established by a timestamped pre-cutoff transcript; 18:30Z is the earliest exact-time issuer release found, not proof that the figures were first spoken then.
No company-issued single-point total-revenue target of exactly $11B was located in the deck; the reported range is a calculation from the stated 2026E revenue and CAGR.
The reviewed sources do not establish broad sell-side consensus for the 2030 model or validate the targets independently.
No Bloom-specific customer, project, order, or deployment connection was found in this onsemi event.
